All stations

Training track · 36 stations · 20 levels · 1616 lessons

Bay Area Union Edition — Sheet Metal, Bridge, Port and Marine

SMART sheet metal workers, the Ironworkers and IUPAT bridge crews with the Pile Drivers of the Carpenters, ILWU longshore and maintenance workers with the PMA training programme and IUOE crane maintenance, and the marine unions: the Inlandboatmen's Union of the ILWU, MEBA and SIU, with the Pile Drivers' commercial divers for the underwater work

SMART's International Training Institute curriculum, Ironworkers IMPACT and OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart R and Subpart M, IUPAT FTI and SSPC practice for bridge coatings, ILWU-PMA training and OSHA 29 CFR 1917 marine terminals, USCG Subchapter M and 33 CFR 156 for the marine side, and OSHA 29 CFR 1910 Subpart T with ADCI consensus standards for commercial diving

One Bay Area tool for four union families: the sheet metal shop and the duct run, the Golden Gate Bridge tower, cable and paint programme, the terminal's cranes, fenders and reefer power, and the water itself: ferries, mooring, oil transfer, and the dive stage down to the piles and the hull.

Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

What it proves

Competency: Work the Bay Area's sheet metal, bridge, port maintenance and marine trades to their unions' standards

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 6 of its 36 stations, against OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart R Steel erection; OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart M Fall protection; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.134 Respiratory protection.

These stations also count toward:

  • Fall Protection (1 of this track's stations count toward it)
  • Lockout/Tagout and the control of hazardous energy (1 of this track's stations count toward it)
  • Crane and Rigging — the lift plan, the load and the landing (1 of this track's stations count toward it)

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: SMART's International Training Institute curriculum, Ironworkers IMPACT and OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart R and Subpart M, IUPAT FTI and SSPC practice for bridge coatings, ILWU-PMA training and OSHA 29 CFR 1917 marine terminals, USCG Subchapter M and 33 CFR 156 for the marine side, and OSHA 29 CFR 1910 Subpart T with ADCI consensus standards for commercial diving. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
